claim: DAN-aSP13 neurons display increased luminescence between 7-10 hours after training with mated females compared to naive males.
source: Notably, flies that had undergone training with mated females displayed a gradual increase of the luminescence signal, which was significantly different from naïve males between 7–10 hr from the onset of training (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by luminescence measurements shown in Figure 1A and described in the text.

claim: Males trained with virgin females do not show increased DAN-aSP13 luminescence compared to naive males.
source: In contrast, control males that had undergone training with virgin females also displayed an increase in luminescence however, it was identical to that in naïve males (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luminescence data from control experiments with virgin females.

claim: The time window of DAN-aSP13 activation (7-10 hours after training onset) is preserved regardless of circadian time of training.
source: That specific time window of DAN-aSP13 activation after onset of training with mated females was preserved in males that were trained in a later circadian time during the day (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing consistent timing across different training schedules.

claim: Males trained for LTM sleep significantly more between 7-10 hours after training onset compared to naive males.
source: Importantly, males that had undergone training for LTM slept significantly more in this time window in comparison to naïve males (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by sleep monitoring data comparing trained and naive males.

claim: Enhancement of post-training sleep occurs between 7-10 hours from the start of training regardless of the circadian time of training.
source: Notably, enhancement of post-training sleep occurs between 7–10 hr from the start of training regardless of the circadian time of training. Males that were trained for LTM in the afternoon instead of the usual morning session, displayed an increased amount of sleep between 7–10 hr after onset of training (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by sleep data from males trained at different times of day.

claim: Males trained for 1 hour to induce STM do not exhibit increased sleep.
source: In contrast, males that were trained for 1 hr to induce STM did not exhibit an increased amount of sleep (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by sleep monitoring data from males trained for short-term memory.

claim: DopR1 mutant males do not display increased post-training sleep despite undergoing the same courtship experience.
source: DopR1 mutant males, although underwent the same courtship experience and courted mated females as vigorously or more than the wild-type males during 6 hr training (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G), neither displayed an increased amount of post-training sleep (Figure 1C) nor formed LTM (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by sleep and courtship data from DopR1 mutant males.

claim: Learning is essential for sleep enhancement in the specific time window after training.
source: Together, these data show that learning is essential for the sleep enhancement in the specific time window after training.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison of wild-type and DopR1 mutant data showing that courtship activity alone is insufficient.

claim: Sleep deprivation between 7-9 and 8-10 hours after training blocks long-term memory.
source: However, males that were deprived of sleep between 7–9 and 8–10 hr had SIs indistinguishable from 0 (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by memory testing data from sleep-deprived males.

claim: Sleep deprivation between 9-11 and 10-12 hours after training does not impair long-term memory.
source: Control males that were trained with mated females and allowed to sleep, and males that were sleep deprived after training between 9–11 and 10–12 hr had normal SIs of approximately 30–40%.
evidence: The claim is supported by memory testing showing normal suppression indices in these groups.

claim: Post-learning sleep is necessary for LTM consolidation.
source: These results show that sleep deprivation between 7–9 hr after the start of training blocks LTM, and thus post-learning sleep is necessary for LTM consolidation.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from sleep deprivation experiments showing memory impairment.

claim: Silencing DAN-aSP13s between 7-9 or 8-10 hours after training abolishes long-term memory.
source: Inhibition of DAN-aSP13s between 7–9 or 8–10 hr, but not between 9–12 hr, after the onset of training abolished LTM. Control males, in which DAN-aSP13s remained functional throughout the assay, had a normal SI between 30–40% (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic silencing experiments showing memory impairment.

claim: Sleep and DAN-aSP13 activity are essential for memory consolidation in the same time window after training.
source: These results show that sleep and DAN-aSP13 activity are essential for memory consolidation in the same time window after training.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from comparing sleep deprivation and DAN-aSP13 silencing experiments.

claim: Activating FB neurons (104y-GAL4) between 5-7 hours after 1 hour training consolidates short-term memory into long-term memory.
source: We found that activating FB neurons (104y-GAL4 > UAS CsChrimson) in the period between 5–7 hr after the onset of training led to a SI of ~ 30%, which is similar to that obtained after LTM training (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic activation experiments showing memory consolidation.

claim: Activating FB neurons at time intervals other than 5-7 hours after training does not consolidate long-term memory.
source: In contrast, males activated at other time intervals or not activated at all failed to consolidate LTM and had SIs that were indistinguishable from 0.
evidence: The claim is supported by optogenetic activation experiments at different time windows.

claim: The temporal window for FB neuron activation to consolidate LTM is identical to that for DAN-aSP13 activation.
source: This temporal window was identical to that observed for DAN-aSP13s activation to consolidate LTM (VT005526-LexA > LexAop-CsChrimson) (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparing optogenetic activation experiments of FB neurons and DAN-aSP13s.

claim: Activating FB neurons while silencing DAN-aSP13s between 5-7 hours after training does not produce long-term memory.
source: When we activated FB neurons (104y-GAL4 > UAS-CsChrimson) while silencing DAN-aSP13s (VT005526-LexA > LexAop-Shits) between 5–7 hr after the onset of training we did not observe LTM (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by combined optogenetic activation and silencing experiments.

claim: Enhancement of sleep after a learning experience that induces STM can consolidate it to LTM in a manner that requires activation of DAN-aSP13s.
source: Taken together, these data show that enhancement of sleep after a learning experience that induces STM can consolidate it to LTM, in a manner that requires activation of DAN-aSP13s.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from sleep induction and DAN-aSP13 manipulation experiments.

claim: Activation of DAN-aSP13s in naive males during normal sleep does not induce courtship suppression towards mated females.
source: This LTM consolidation is a specific effect of DAN-aSP13s activation after training since activation of DAN-aSP13s (VT005526-LexA > LexAop-CsChrimson) in naïve males between 5–7 hr when they normally display a significant amount of sleep does not induce courtship suppression towards mated females and thus 'courtship LTM' (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by control experiments activating DAN-aSP13s in naive males.

claim: Local activation of FB neurons elicits an excitatory response in DAN-aSP13s.
source: Local activation of FB neurons elicited an excitatory response in DAN-aSP13s (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by calcium imaging data showing increased activity in DAN-aSP13s upon FB neuron activation.

claim: Activation of the vFB layer induces excitatory responses in DAN-aSP13s.
source: Surprisingly, activation of the dFB layer, which has been recently implicated in homeostatic sleep regulation (Donlea et al., 2011), resulted in a mixture of small inhibitory and excitatory responses (Figure 3C), whereas activation of the vFB layer induced excitatory responses in DAN-aSP13s (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by layer-specific optogenetic activation and calcium imaging experiments.

claim: Activation of the dFB layer results in a mixture of small inhibitory and excitatory responses in DAN-aSP13s.
source: Surprisingly, activation of the dFB layer, which has been recently implicated in homeostatic sleep regulation (Donlea et al., 2011), resulted in a mixture of small inhibitory and excitatory responses (Figure 3C), whereas activation of the vFB layer induced excitatory responses in DAN-aSP13s (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by layer-specific optogenetic activation and calcium imaging experiments.

claim: Activation of the mFB layer has no effect on DAN-aSP13 activity.
source: Activation of the mFB had no effect on DAN-aSP13 activity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by calcium imaging data showing no response in DAN-aSP13s upon mFB activation.

claim: Neurons that project to the vFB and potentially the dFB layers provide excitatory input onto DAN-aSP13s.
source: These data show that neurons that project to the vFB and potentially the dFB layers provide an excitatory input onto DAN-aSP13s and may thus have a role in LTM consolidation.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from layer-specific activation experiments.

claim: Thermogenetic activation of dFB neurons over 24 hours results in increased sleep.
source: As previously reported, thermogenetic activation of dFB over a 24 hr time period resulted in an increased amount of sleep (R23E10-GAL4 > UAS-TrpA1) (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by sleep monitoring data and cites previous reports.

claim: Activation of vFB neurons robustly induces daytime sleep.
source: We found that activation of vFB (VT036875-GAL4 > UAS-TrpA1; VT036875-GAL4 > UAS-TrpA1, R58E02-GAL80; SS057264-GAL4 > UAS-TrpA1) also robustly induced day time sleep (Figure 4B,C,D) in comparison to the genetic control (pBDP-GAL4 > UAS-TrpA1) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by sleep monitoring data from multiple vFB-specific driver lines.

claim: Activation of dFB neurons does not elicit calcium changes in DAN-aSP13s.
source: Activation of dFB neurons did not elicit calcium changes in DAN-aSP13s (Figure 4A) however, activation of vFB neurons elicited a robust increase of calcium levels in DAN-aSP13s (Figure 4B,C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by calcium imaging experiments showing no response in DAN-aSP13s upon dFB activation.

claim: Activation of vFB neurons elicits a robust increase of calcium levels in DAN-aSP13s.
source: Activation of dFB neurons did not elicit calcium changes in DAN-aSP13s (Figure 4A) however, activation of vFB neurons elicited a robust increase of calcium levels in DAN-aSP13s (Figure 4B,C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by calcium imaging experiments showing increased activity in DAN-aSP13s upon vFB activation.

claim: vFB neurons provide excitatory input onto DAN-aSP13s.
source: These data show that neurons in the vFB provide excitatory input onto DAN-aSP13s.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from calcium imaging experiments showing increased DAN-aSP13 activity upon vFB activation.

claim: Optogenetic activation of dFB neurons between 5-7 hours after 1 hour training does not lead to LTM consolidation.
source: Consistent with the functional connectivity results, optogenetic activation of dFB neurons (R23E10-GAL4 > UAS-CsChrimson) between 5–7 hr after a 1 hr training period did not lead to LTM consolidation.
evidence: The claim is supported by memory testing data from optogenetic activation experiments.

claim: Activation of vFB neurons between 5-7 hours after 1 hour training fully consolidates STM to LTM.
source: However, activation of either a combination of dFB and vFB neurons (104y-GAL4 > UAS-CsChrimson) or just the vFB neurons (VT036875-GAL4 > UAS-CsChrimson; VT036875-GAL4 > UAS-CsChrimson, R58E02-GAL80; SS057264-GAL4 > UAS-CsChrimson) in that same time window fully consolidated STM to LTM (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by memory testing data from optogenetic activation experiments.

claim: Silencing dFB neurons between 7-10 hours after 6 hour training does not affect LTM persistence.
source: In addition, silencing of dFB neurons (R23E10-GAL4 > UAS-Shits) in the period between 7–10 hr after the onset of a 6 hr training period did not affect LTM persistence, while silencing of a combination of dFB and vFB or just the vFB neurons (VT036875-GAL4 > UAS-Shits; SS057264-GAL4 > UAS-Shits and 104y-GAL4 > UAS-Shits) in the same time window strongly impaired LTM consolidation (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by memory testing data from optogenetic silencing experiments.

claim: Silencing vFB neurons between 7-10 hours after 6 hour training strongly impairs LTM consolidation.
source: In addition, silencing of dFB neurons (R23E10-GAL4 > UAS-Shits) in the period between 7–10 hr after the onset of a 6 hr training period did not affect LTM persistence, while silencing of a combination of dFB and vFB or just the vFB neurons (VT036875-GAL4 > UAS-Shits; SS057264-GAL4 > UAS-Shits and 104y-GAL4 > UAS-Shits) in the same time window strongly impaired LTM consolidation (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by memory testing data from optogenetic silencing experiments.

claim: A class of sleep-promoting neurons in the vFB layer is necessary and sufficient to consolidate LTM during post-learning sleep.
source: These results show that a class of sleep-promoting neurons in the vFB layer of the 104y-FB expression pattern is necessary and sufficient to consolidate LTM during post-learning sleep.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from optogenetic activation and silencing experiments of vFB neurons.

claim: dFB neurons, although they promote sleep, have no role in courtship LTM consolidation.
source: dFB neurons, although they promote sleep, appear to have no role in courtship LTM consolidation.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from experiments showing dFB neurons promote sleep but their manipulation does not affect courtship LTM.

claim: Activity of DAN-aSP13s is necessary and sufficient for STM acquisition via the dopamine receptor DopR1 in γKCs.
source: We previously established that activity of the dopaminergic aSP13 neurons (DAN-aSP13s) is necessary and sufficient for STM acquisition via the dopamine receptor DopR1 in the γ neurons of the mushroom body known as Kenyon Cells (γKCs) (Keleman et al., 2012), a neuropil in the Drosophila central brain critical for memory formation (Heisenberg et al., 1985).
evidence: The claim cites previous work by the authors and others.

claim: Activity of DAN-aSP13s is essential for the consolidation of courtship STM to LTM in a discrete time window after learning.
source: Moreover, we recently demonstrated that the activity of the same DAN-aSP13s is also essential for the consolidation of courtship STM to LTM. This requirement is observed in a discrete time window after learning, and it is mediated via the dopamine receptor DopR1 in the γKCs (Krüttner et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim cites previous work by the authors.

claim: Sleep in Drosophila exhibits almost all the hallmarks of sleep in mammals, including homeostatic regulation, diminished behavioral responsiveness, and different sleep stages.
source: Sleep in Drosophila exhibits almost all the hallmarks of sleep in mammals, including homeostatic regulation, diminished behavioral responsiveness, and the existence of different sleep stages as characterized by distinct electrophysiological signatures (Dissel et al., 2015a; Yap et al., 2017; van Alphen et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim cites multiple studies characterizing sleep in Drosophila.

claim: Sleep deprivation before and after learning impairs mnemonic performance in Drosophila.
source: Recently, a link between sleep and LTM has been established: sleep deprivation before and after learning impairs mnemonic performance (Ganguly-Fitzgerald et al., 2006; Seugnet et al., 2008; Seugnet et al., 2009), whereas sleep induction enhances memory formation and retention in wild-type (Donlea et al., 2011) and restores memory in memory mutant flies (Dissel et al., 2015b).
evidence: The claim cites multiple studies showing effects of sleep manipulation on memory in Drosophila.

claim: Sleep induction enhances memory formation and retention in wild-type Drosophila.
source: Recently, a link between sleep and LTM has been established: sleep deprivation before and after learning impairs mnemonic performance (Ganguly-Fitzgerald et al., 2006; Seugnet et al., 2008; Seugnet et al., 2009), whereas sleep induction enhances memory formation and retention in wild-type (Donlea et al., 2011) and restores memory in memory mutant flies (Dissel et al., 2015b).
evidence: The claim cites a study showing sleep induction enhances memory.

claim: Flies exposed to a socially enriched environment, including courtship learning, exhibit an increased amount of sleep.
source: Moreover, flies that were exposed to a socially enriched environment, including courtship learning, exhibit an increased amount of sleep (Ganguly-Fitzgerald et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim cites a study showing social enrichment increases sleep.

claim: STM is thought to rely on protein synthesis-independent covalent modifications and changes in weight of existing synaptic connections.
source: STM is thought to rely on protein synthesis-independent covalent modifications and changes in weight of existing synaptic connections, whereas LTM is believed to reflect protein synthesis-dependent structural changes in specific synapses (Kandel, 2001).
evidence: The claim cites established knowledge about the molecular basis of STM.

claim: LTM is believed to reflect protein synthesis-dependent structural changes in specific synapses.
source: STM is thought to rely on protein synthesis-independent covalent modifications and changes in weight of existing synaptic connections, whereas LTM is believed to reflect protein synthesis-dependent structural changes in specific synapses (Kandel, 2001).
evidence: The claim cites established knowledge about the molecular basis of LTM.

claim: Sleep has a beneficial effect on memory in various learning tasks in vertebrates.
source: Numerous studies in vertebrates suggest that sleep has a beneficial effect on memory in various learning tasks (Marshall and Born, 2007; Smith, 2001).
evidence: The claim cites studies showing sleep benefits memory in vertebrates.

claim: Insufficient sleep impairs cognitive functions such as memory formation and retention in humans and rodents.
source: Studies in humans and rodents have shown that an insufficient amount of sleep impairs cognitive functions such as memory formation and retention, while an ample amount of sleep after a learning experience supports memory storage (Goel et al., 2009; Diekelmann and Born, 2010).
evidence: The claim cites studies showing sleep deprivation impairs memory.

claim: Ample sleep after a learning experience supports memory storage in humans and rodents.
source: Studies in humans and rodents have shown that an insufficient amount of sleep impairs cognitive functions such as memory formation and retention, while an ample amount of sleep after a learning experience supports memory storage (Goel et al., 2009; Diekelmann and Born, 2010).
evidence: The claim cites studies showing adequate sleep supports memory.

claim: Animals, including humans, exhibit enhanced amount and quality of sleep after experiencing a novel or enriched environment.
source: In addition, several studies have found that animals, including humans, exhibit an enhanced amount and quality of sleep after experiencing a novel or enriched environment (Gais et al., 2002; Smith and Wong, 1991; Walker and Stickgold, 2006).
evidence: The claim cites multiple studies showing environmental enrichment increases sleep.

claim: Consolidation of courtship long-term memory in Drosophila is mediated by reactivation during sleep of dopaminergic neurons that were earlier involved in memory acquisition.
source: Here, we show that consolidation of courtship long-term memory in Drosophila is mediated by reactivation during sleep of dopaminergic neurons that were earlier involved in memory acquisition.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: Specific fan-shaped body neurons induce sleep after the learning experience and activate dopaminergic neurons for memory consolidation.
source: We identify specific fan-shaped body neurons that induce sleep after the learning experience and activate dopaminergic neurons for memory consolidation.
evidence: This is a main finding of the study, supported by optogenetic and calcium imaging experiments.

claim: During a prolonged learning experience, γKCs and DAN-aSP13s are repeatedly activated by olfactory and behavioral cues presented by an unreceptive female.
source: During a prolonged learning experience, γKCs and DAN-aSP13s are repeatedly activated by olfactory and behavioral cues presented by an unreceptive female, respectively.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model in the Discussion section, based on the experimental findings.

claim: An extended learning experience generates a learning-dependent sleep drive that is transmitted to vFB neurons.
source: Whereas prolonged wakefulness leads to an increase in homeostatic sleep drive in ellipsoid body neurons that in turn is conveyed to dFB (Liu et al., 2016), we hypothesize that an extended learning experience generates a learning-dependent sleep drive that is transmitted to vFB.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed in the Discussion, based on the experimental findings and cited work.

claim: vFB neurons enhance sleep after learning and provide excitatory input back on DAN-aSP13s.
source: In turn, the vFB neurons enhance sleep after learning and provide an excitatory input back on DAN-aSP13s.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model, supported by sleep induction and calcium imaging experiments.

claim: Dopamine released upon DAN-aSP13 reactivation stimulates molecular processes in γKCs that involve protein synthesis essential for LTM formation.
source: Dopamine released upon DAN-aSP13 reactivation stimulates molecular processes in γKCs (Krüttner et al., 2015) that are different from those engaged during STM acquisition and involve protein synthesis that is essential for LTM formation and persistence.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model, based on the current findings and cited previous work.

claim: Post-learning neuronal activity of dopaminergic hippocampal inputs from the VTA has been implicated in consolidation of fear memory in rodents.
source: Post-learning neuronal activity of the dopaminergic hippocampal inputs from the Ventral Tagmental Area (VTA) has been implicated in the consolidation of fear memory in rodents. Interestingly, this activity is critical during a discrete time window after learning (Rossato et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim cites a study in rodents showing similar post-learning dopaminergic activity.

claim: Post-learning activity of VTA dopamine neurons has been implicated in reactivation during sleep of hippocampal cells involved in encoding spatial experience.
source: Post-learning activity of the VTA dopamine neurons has been also implicated in the reactivation during sleep of the hippocampal cells involved earlier in encoding of the spatial experience (Gomperts et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim cites a study showing dopaminergic involvement in sleep-dependent reactivation.

claim: Reactivation during sleep of dopamine neurons previously active during memory acquisition ensures that only sufficiently salient or persistent experiences become long-lasting memories.
source: We propose that reactivation during sleep of the dopamine neurons that were previously active during memory acquisition ensures that spurious experiences are not admitted into LTM storage and thus only experiences that are either sufficiently salient or persistent become long-lasting memories.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed in the Discussion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Reactivation of DAN-aSP13s during post-learning sleep enhances reactivation of γKCs and cognate MBON-M6.
source: Specifically, reactivation of DAN-aSP13s during post-learning sleep enhances reactivation of the γKCs and cognate MBON-M6, which together with DAN-aSP13s form a recurrent circuit necessary for courtship memory acquisition (Zhao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the current findings and cited work on circuit organization.

claim: Artificial activation of DAN-aSP13s increases wakefulness.
source: Artificial activation of DAN-aSP13s has been shown to increase wakefulness (Sitaraman et al., 2015a).
evidence: The claim cites a study showing DAN-aSP13 activation promotes wakefulness.

claim: Activation of DAN-aSP13s by vFB neurons during sleep is qualitatively different from direct optogenetic or thermogenetic activation.
source: These results suggest that activation of DAN-aSP13s by vFB neurons during sleep is qualitatively different from a direct optogenetic or thermogenetic activation used in previous studies.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain why vFB activation doesn't promote wakefulness despite activating DAN-aSP13s.

claim: vFB neurons are distinct from dFB neurons that regulate sleep homeostasis.
source: We have identified here a class of sleep-promoting neurons in the ventral layer of FB that are distinct from the well-studied sleep-promoting neurons in the dorsal layer of FB, which regulate sleep homeostasis (Donlea et al., 2011; Donlea et al., 2014; Pimentel et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental findings and cites previous work on dFB neurons.

claim: dFB and vFB neurons promote distinct components of sleep that have different functions.
source: Given that vFB neurons enhance sleep and activate DAN-aSP13s for LTM consolidation, whereas dFB neurons are neither necessary nor sufficient for LTM consolidation, we hypothesize that dFB and vFB neurons promote distinct components of sleep that have different functions.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on the differential effects of dFB and vFB manipulation.

claim: Homeostatic sleep facilitates memory encoding by downscaling synaptic weights and clearing metabolites from the brain.
source: Homeostatic sleep is thought to facilitate memory encoding by downscaling synaptic weights and clearing metabolites from the brain accumulated during wakefulness (Bushey et al., 2011; Xie et al., 2013; Tononi and Cirelli, 2014).
evidence: The claim cites studies proposing functions of homeostatic sleep.

claim: Learning-dependent sleep facilitates memory consolidation by strengthening synaptic connections engaged during memory acquisition.
source: In contrast, the function of learning-dependent sleep might be to facilitate memory consolidation by strengthening synaptic connections that were engaged earlier during memory acquisition (Frank, 2012).
evidence: The claim cites a study proposing a function for learning-dependent sleep.

claim: Sleep in flies exhibits sleep stages characterized by distinct electrophysiological signatures.
source: Recent studies have implied that sleep in flies, as in humans and rodents, exhibits sleep stages characterized by distinct electrophysiological signatures (Yap et al., 2017; van Alphen et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim cites studies characterizing sleep stages in Drosophila.

claim: Sleep induced by dFB neuron activation has a simpler oscillatory pattern than sleep induced by activation of both dFB and vFB neurons.
source: Interestingly, the signature of sleep that is induced by activation of the dFB neurons seems to have a simpler oscillatory pattern, recorded by local field potentials, than sleep that is induced by activation of the FB neurons comprising both dFB and vFB neurons (Yap et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim cites a study showing different electrophysiological signatures for different types of sleep.

claim: Courtship learning is a multisensory form of learning that requires selective attention.
source: Courtship learning is a multisensory form of learning that requires selective attention of a male to associate multiple learning cues presented by the mated female with the outcome of his own behavior (Kirszenblat and van Swinderen, 2015).
evidence: The claim describes the nature of courtship learning and cites a relevant study.

claim: Sleep affects spatial memory but has no role in simple learning paradigms like proboscis extension in bees.
source: Accordingly, studies in bees have shown that sleep affects a complex form of learning such as spatial memory but has no role in the simple learning paradigm of proboscis extension (Vorster and Born, 2015).
evidence: The claim cites a study showing differential effects of sleep on different types of learning.

claim: This work establishes a functional link between a novel class of sleep-promoting neurons in the FB, post-learning reactivation of dopaminergic neurons, and consolidation of courtship LTM.
source: In this work, we establish a functional link between a novel class of sleep-promoting neurons in the FB, post-learning reactivation of dopaminergic neurons and consolidation of courtship LTM.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings of the study.

claim: The data suggest that sleep promoting vFB neurons mediate learning-dependent regulation of sleep distinct from homeostatic control facilitated by dFB neurons.
source: Moreover, our data suggest that sleep promoting vFB neurons mediate a learning-dependent regulation of sleep that is distinct from the homeostatic control which is facilitated by dFB neurons (Liu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings and cited work.

claim: This work uncovers a causal link between sleep-mediated neuronal reactivation and LTM consolidation in Drosophila.
source: Thus, we uncover a causal link between sleep-mediated neuronal reactivation and LTM consolidation in Drosophila.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main contribution of the study.

claim: Courtship LTM in Drosophila is established as a tractable model to investigate mechanisms linking learning-dependent sleep, neuronal reactivation, and LTM consolidation.
source: In addition, we establish courtship LTM in Drosophila as a tractable model to investigate the mechanisms that link learning-dependent sleep, neuronal reactivation and LTM consolidation.
evidence: This is a statement about the broader impact and utility of the study.

claim: Naive Drosophila males eagerly court both virgin and mated females.
source: Naive Drosophila males eagerly court both virgin and mated females, which are generally receptive and unreceptive, respectively.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila courtship behavior.

claim: After being repeatedly rejected by mated females, males become less likely to court other mated females.
source: However, after being repeatedly rejected by mated females, males become less likely to court other mated females (Ejima et al., 2005; Keleman et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the courtship conditioning learning paradigm and cites relevant studies.

claim: The mushroom body is a neuropil in the Drosophila central brain critical for memory formation.
source: We previously established that activity of the dopaminergic aSP13 neurons (DAN-aSP13s) is necessary and sufficient for STM acquisition via the dopamine receptor DopR1 in the γ neurons of the mushroom body known as Kenyon Cells (γKCs) (Keleman et al., 2012), a neuropil in the Drosophila central brain critical for memory formation (Heisenberg et al., 1985).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mushroom body and cites a foundational study.

claim: One potential site of learning-dependent sleep drive is the MB neurons since they have been implicated in both memory formation and sleep regulation.
source: We believe that one potential site of a learning-dependent sleep drive are the MB neurons since they have been implicated in both memory formation (Heisenberg et al., 1985) and sleep regulation (Sitaraman et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on cited literature about MB function.

claim: Prolonged wakefulness leads to an increase in homeostatic sleep drive in ellipsoid body neurons that is conveyed to dFB.
source: Whereas prolonged wakefulness leads to an increase in homeostatic sleep drive in ellipsoid body neurons that in turn is conveyed to dFB (Liu et al., 2016), we hypothesize that an extended learning experience generates a learning-dependent sleep drive that is transmitted to vFB.
evidence: The claim cites a study describing homeostatic sleep regulation.
